decisive_items: choking episode while eating yellowtail fish approximately 11 months prior to presentation
obstructive pneumonia surrounding edematous area in the right lower lung
obstruction of the basal segmental bronchus's lumen with edematous formation in the right lower lung
response.rationale: Choking episode plus bronchial obstruction and obstructive pneumonia strongly indicate aspirated foreign body localized to the right lower lung; R1C adds the anatomical specificity supported by imaging and bronchoscopy.

rejected.why: Pneumonia is too generic and lacks the foreign body mechanism.
COPD does not explain bronchial obstruction or choking episode.
Captures aspiration but omits the specific right lower lung localization.
Pulmonary embolism lacks supporting imaging or clinical features.
Lung cancer contradicted by choking episode and obstructive findings; tumor markers normal.
Obstructive pneumonia is a consequence, not the underlying cause.
Chronic bronchitis does not account for bronchial obstruction or aspiration.
Correct mechanism but less specific than R1C regarding location.
Pulmonary abscess not supported by imaging or labs.
